## Appearance

Thirza is a tall, slender woman with a lean figure defined by sharp contours and angles. She wears her dark hair, which has increasingly silvered over time with graying strands, coiled in a firm, tight bun at the back. Her physical features include lined cheeks, rough, labor-calloused hands, and failing eyesight that, while no longer at risk of complete blindness, remains permanently limited.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Surprised P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015), [v2 VIII Thirza Adopts Twins P3](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0003), [v2 XII A Jonah Day P39](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0039), [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P4](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0004), [v2 XV The Beginning of Vacation P43](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0043), +2 more_

## Personality

Thirza Abernethy is a composed, rational, and practical individual who maintains an unyielding sense of morality and a strict commitment to duty. Though characterized as rigid, stern, and restrained, she exhibits a softer and kinder demeanor over time, alongside a subtle sense of humor and a mellowing presence. She routinely attaches moral lessons to her speech, refrains from expressing opinions on ministers on principle, and harbors a dislike for cats. Possessing a pessimistic streak and an anxious protectiveness over those she cares for, she finds intense displays of emotion improper. Additionally, she is skilled in domestic crafts, including rug-making, braided rug construction, and producing renowned currant wine and plum preserves.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Surprised P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 CHAPTER IV. ## History

Thirza Abernethy lived at [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) for sixty years, having moved there upon reaching adulthood. She wallpapered a spare bedroom four years prior to her story beginning with the assistance of her brother, [Obed Abernethy](../character/obed-abernethy.md). When [Obed](../character/obed-abernethy.md) set out to pick up an orphan boy to help on their farm, Thirza initially defended his decision to their inquisitive neighbor, [Agatha Sowerby](../character/agatha-sowerby.md). However, upon discovering that a young girl named [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) was sent instead, Thirza originally insisted on sending her back, though she delayed the decision after encountering Mrs. [Scobie](../character/scobie.md) and ultimately agreed with [Obed](../character/obed-abernethy.md) to keep [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md). Thirza took full responsibility for Nell's religious upbringing and began providing for her education, though she strictly managed Nell's dress and imagination, including scolding her for decorating a hat for church and cutting her hair short after [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) accidentally dyed it green. Remorseful after falsely accusing [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) of stealing an amethyst brooch inherited from her mother, Thirza forged a deeper bond with the girl, later expressing her rare fondness to [Obed](../character/obed-abernethy.md). Following Obed's sudden death and receiving news that her own vision was severely failing, Thirza planned to sell [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) until [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) relinquished a college scholarship to stay and teach locally. Later, out of a sense of duty, Thirza agreed to welcome the orphaned Farrow twins into [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) and permanently raised them alongside [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md). As her vision and health waned in her later years, Thirza invited [Agatha Sowerby](../character/agatha-sowerby.md) to live with them so [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) could pursue her higher education at [Wexcombe College](../codex/places.md#wexcombe-college).

## Quotes

> "At minimum, provide me with someone native born. A risk will exist, regardless of whom we obtain. Nevertheless, my mind will be more at ease and my night’s sleep will be sounder if we obtain a born Canadian."
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Surprised P23](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0023)

> "No. A boy is what we need to assist Obed on the farm. To us, a girl would be useless. Remove your hat. On the hall table, I’ll place it along with your bag."
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised P30](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0030)

> "Now, strip off your clothes as fast as possible and get into bed. In a little while, I’ll return to fetch the candle. Leaving you to extinguish it on your own is too risky. It’s probable you’d burn down the house."
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised P44](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0044)

> "Obed Abernethy, my belief is that you have been enchanted by that child! It is as clear as day to me that your desire is to retain her."
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised P61](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0061)

> "Obed Abernethy, my surprise at you is great. Though aware of Nell’s terrible conduct, you still defend her! Next, I expect you will claim that no punishment whatsoever should be given to her!"
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology P2](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0002)

## Relationships

### [Agatha Sowerby](../character/agatha-sowerby.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/agatha-sowerby--thirza-abernethy.md)

[Agatha Sowerby](../character/agatha-sowerby.md) and Thirza Abernethy are longstanding friends and neighbors who regularly visit each other's homes. [Agatha](../character/agatha-sowerby.md) frequently drops by [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) with gossip, warnings, and sharp opinions on Thirza's household management. Their friendship encounters occasional strain over Agatha's blunt nature, such as when [Agatha](../character/agatha-sowerby.md) insulted Nell's appearance, forcing Thirza to demand an apology from [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) to preserve peace between the households.

### [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/nell-harcourt--thirza-abernethy.md)

Thirza serves as a guardian, mentor, and maternal figure to [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) after taking her in at [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters). Though initially strict about Nell's manners, dress, and religious upbringing, Thirza quickly grows fond of the girl and decides to keep her despite an initial mix-up. Over time, their bond deepens into a close mother-and-daughter dynamic as Thirza guides [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) through childhood misadventures and school achievements.

### [Pembroke](../character/pembroke.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/pembroke--thirza-abernethy.md)

Mrs. [Pembroke](../character/pembroke.md) is a local acquaintance whose daughter Isolde is close friends with [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md). Their relationship faces temporary friction when Mrs. [Pembroke](../character/pembroke.md) misjudges an incident where [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) accidentally serves Isolde homemade wine, though Mrs. [Pembroke](../character/pembroke.md) later apologizes and restores good relations between the families.
